entries.title_fr: European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) - Coopération européenne pour la normalisation spatiale
entries.text_en: The European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) is a cornerstone of Europe’s space industry, ensuring consistency and reliability across all space missions developed on the continent. Launched in 1993 and officially adopted by the European Space Agency (ESA) the following year, the ECSS was created to unify disparate standardization efforts under a single, coherent framework. Before its establishment, European space projects relied on fragmented and often conflicting standards, leading to inefficiencies and increased costs. By replacing ESA’s older Procedures, Specifications and Standards (PSS) system, the ECSS introduced a streamlined approach that now governs everything from project management to engineering and product assurance. Today, the ECSS system includes 144 active standards, meticulously structured into eight branches that cover disciplines such as system engineering, product assurance, and space sustainability. Managed by ESA’s Requirement and Standard Division at ESTEC in the Netherlands, the ECSS collaborates with international organizations to harmonize global space standards, ensuring Europe remains a leader in safe, sustainable, and cost-effective space exploration.
